item.title: 'Embarrassing': Wasim Akram slams Pakistan's shocking mid-tour changes
item.description: The former Pakistan captain also asked the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to give the domestic system enough time to produce results instead of making regular changes. Akram also stressed the need to strengthen cricket at the grassroots level. He called for greater focus on club, school and college cricket to ensure a steady supply of talent.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Countries where you can buy iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max cheaper than India
item.description: Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models have officially launched worldwide. These devices feature the powerful A20 Pro chip and improved camera technology. Pricing for these flagship iPhones varies considerably across different countries. The United States offers the most affordable purchase option for both models. India's pricing reflects higher local taxes and import duties on electronics.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 'Smashed heads with stone': Man kills wife, 3 daughters in Jaipur
item.description: A man allegedly killed his wife and three daughters in Jaipur's Kardhani area. He reportedly used a stone to strike them on their heads while they slept. The accused then collected milk from a deliveryman before fleeing the scene. Police are searching for the suspect and investigating a possible family dispute. The victims were found at their home in Govind Vatika early Friday morning.
item.dc:creator: DISHANK PUROHIT

item.title: Elon Musk feels 'chess will be fully solved one day'; what does Carlsen think?
item.description: Elon Musk believes chess will eventually be fully solved by AI, drawing comparisons with checkers. Magnus Carlsen was less certain, saying he isn't a computer expert but noting chess is already “semi-solved” as a likely draw. Carlsen also praised AI for making chess more accessible, while backing the Global Chess League’s exciting team format and enjoying his visits to India.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Las Vegas developers buy 940 acres of former federal desert for $94 million; 6,000-home community planned
item.description: A large federal desert parcel near Las Vegas will become Monument Hills, a new master-planned community. This development will feature up to 6,000 homes and various amenities for residents. The $94 million land deal is the largest BLM transaction in the valley for decades. Proceeds from the sale will fund projects across Nevada, including parks and education. First homes are anticipated to be available around spring 2028.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Dating to 1898, Nipomo's oldest church donated after 128 years to become a community hub
item.description: A historic church in Nipomo, California, dating to 1898, has been donated to the Dana Adobe and Cultural Center by its owners, John and Rebecca Prewett. The building will be developed into a museum, event venue and “Visit Nipomo” centre, while Calvary Church will continue holding Sunday services there.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max go on pre-order tomorrow: 9 biggest features to know
item.description: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are priced from Rs 1,64,900 and Rs 1,79,900 in India. The new Pro models bring a variable aperture main camera, Pro controls, Apple Reference Image, the 2nm A20 Pro chip, a bigger vapour chamber and up to 43 hours of video playback. Pre-orders start September 12, with sales from September 18. Here are the nine features that you should know of before ordering one.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Belize Reef Restoration Effort: Lisa Carne revives storm-hit corals; project outplants 100,000 fragments
item.description: In 2001, Hurricane Iris wreaked havoc on Belize's coral reefs, sparking an innovative restoration effort. Marine biologist Lisa Carne took the lead in replanting coral fragments, which were often neglected. Through her organization, Fragments of Hope, more than 100,000 corals have been successfully restored, resulting in a remarkable boost in coral coverage and marine biodiversity.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: 'My name was not even in the FIR': Former India cricketer’s 22-year ordeal
item.description: After two decades in legal turmoil, former Indian cricketer Jacob Martin has finally been acquitted of all charges related to a 2004 case of forgery and cheating. The court's ruling highlighted the absence of credible evidence against Martin, allowing him to close this challenging chapter of his life and career. He can now look forward to a brighter future, free from the shadows of this protracted legal battle.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: US-based couple flags ‘scam’ at Delhi airport, authorities respond
item.description: A US-based Indian couple alleged passport scanning of their young children at Delhi airport. Staff scanned multiple family passports after one purchase, claiming to check for offers. The couple raised concerns about data collection and potential misuse of personal information. Airport authorities have acknowledged the allegation and promised a thorough investigation. Exemplary action will be taken if the allegations are found to be true.
item.dc:creator: HADI KHAN

item.title: Bank delays release of deceased wife's savings to elderly man; ordered to pay Rs 15K
item.description: A Kerala consumer commission ordered Bank of India to pay compensation for service deficiency. The bank delayed releasing a deceased woman's savings to her elderly husband. The commission found the bank's procedures unnecessarily burdensome and lacking clear communication. The bank failed to prove its defense regarding an unsigned application. The elderly man suffered financial hardship and mental agony due to the bank's actions.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Quote of the day by Brad Pitt on self-discovery; actor reflects on faith and identity
item.description: Brad Pitt openly reflects on his transformative journey away from a conservative religious upbringing. He emphasizes that this shift was an empowering journey of self-discovery rather than a simple abandonment of faith. His experiences resonate deeply with those grappling with their own belief systems, revealing the power of trusting one’s abilities to confront life’s adversities. Pitt's story underscores the value of introspection and personal agency in shaping one’s path.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: 'Mirzapur The Movie' BO Day 8 [LIVE]: Pankaj Tripathi film eyes Rs 150 crore
item.description: 'Mirzapur The Movie' is edging closer to a major box office milestone as it enters Day 8, with its India net collection standing at Rs. 149.26 crore after crossing Rs. 148 crore by the end of Day 7. The Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal and Ravi Kishan starrer is now less than a crore away from the Rs. 150 mark, even as Akshay Kumar and Saif Ali Khan's 'Haiwaan' opens in theatres. Worldwide, the film has already surpassed Rs. 212 crore.

item.title: Watch: Fed up over poor network, villagers tie technician with mobile tower
item.description: Villagers held a mobile tower technician captive for two hours in Fatehpur district. They were frustrated with poor mobile connectivity for approximately two years. Police intervened and rescued the technician after being alerted by another villager. An FIR was registered against unknown villagers following the technician's complaint. Investigations are currently underway regarding the unusual incident.
item.dc:creator: KAPIL DIXIT

item.title: Miami flight overrun: Plane touched down at nearly 300 kmph despite high-speed warning
item.description: A 21 Air Boeing 767 touched down at Miami International Airport at an alarming speed of nearly 300 kmph. As the crew attempted to execute a go-around following the landing, they had neglected to deploy the speed brakes, leading to automated alerts about the steep descent and proximity to the ground. Investigators are now analyzing the flight data and cockpit voice recordings to uncover further insights regarding this incident.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Catastrophic failure: Bangladesh tank blast puts Chinese military hardware under spotlight
item.description: A Chinese-origin tank exploded during an exercise, killing two soldiers and injuring another. This incident follows other nations reporting issues with Chinese military equipment. Several countries have expressed dissatisfaction with Chinese defense system capabilities. China remains a major global arms supplier despite these persistent quality complaints. Bangladesh is still considering purchasing Chinese fighter jets despite past equipment problems.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV

item.title: Saif Ali Khan's Pataudi Palace: Inside 'Haiwaan' actor's ancestral home
item.description: The Pataudi Palace, an ancestral estate of Saif Ali Khan, spans ten acres in Gurugram. This imposing structure, built in the 1930s, showcases royal heritage and unique architecture. Ibrahim Kothi, once home to Tiger Pataudi, features a dome inspired by the Sanchi Stupa. Saif Ali Khan repurchased the leased estate in 2014, returning it to family ownership. The palace remains a significant symbol of the Pataudi family's rich history.
item.dc:creator: etimes.in

item.title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu recalls myositis battle: 'I had no control'
item.description: Samantha Ruth Prabhu opened up about her life after being diagnosed with myositis, a condition that deeply affected her self-esteem and personal identity. She discovered strength, hope, and faith while navigating through the struggles of her illness. Additionally, she shared the joyful news of her pregnancy during the shooting of a music video, eagerly looking forward to the arrival of her first child.

item.title: Karnataka govt limits Vande Mataram to 2 stanzas, barring VVIP functions
item.description: Karnataka's Congress government has ordered singing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram. This directive applies to state government programmes and functions held across Karnataka. The decision follows a Union home ministry guideline for singing all six stanzas. The state government aims for uniformity and appropriate protocol during national song renditions. This move occurs amidst a political controversy surrounding the national song's singing.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: ED raids Ramnandi Hotels across 9 locations in alleged Rs 132-crore bank fraud case
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate searched nine locations across three states in an alleged bank fraud case. Ramnandi Hotels and Resorts Ltd is accused of diverting Rs 58 crore from bank loans. The company allegedly used fake reports and personal guarantees to secure these funds. Five pledged properties were reportedly sold at undervalued prices recently. The agency suspects these actions aimed to prevent asset attachment and recover crime proceeds.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Customer complaint over Shoppers Stop carry bag charges rejected; fined Rs 10K
item.description: A consumer commission dismissed a complaint against Shoppers Stop regarding a paper bag charge. The commission found the case frivolous and imposed exemplary costs on the complainant. The complainant had previously filed a similar case against the retailer for a carry bag fee. The commission noted the complainant's history of filing multiple consumer complaints. This ruling highlights the misuse of consumer protection laws for personal gain.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Collector makes Thar, Fortuner owners take road safety pledge, video goes viral
item.description: The Daman administration organized a road safety event for SUV owners. Mahindra Thar and Toyota Fortuner owners participated in a pledge. This initiative aims to promote responsible driving and road safety awareness. The event featured a rally and a road safety pledge administered by the district collector. It addresses ongoing online discussions regarding the image of these popular vehicles.
item.dc:creator: HADI KHAN

item.title: Al-Falah docs 1st tested bombs inside university, then in Aravalis: NIA
item.description: NIA chargesheet details terror module progression from fertilizer explosives to IEDs. Doctors allegedly tested explosive mixtures and firearms in isolated locations. Weapons were procured using funds routed through a university doctor. Rented premises stored chemicals, equipment, and explosives away from public view. A major cache of ammonium nitrate was seized before the Red Fort blast.
